# 1039—BOUILLABAISSE A LA MARSEILLAISE

## Ingredients

- 2 lbs. fish (rascasse, chapon, dory, fiélas, boudreuil, spiny lobster, red mullet, gurnet)
- 1 small onion
- chopped white of 1 leek
- 1 small, peeled, pressed and chopped tomato
- 2 crushed cloves of garlic
- a large pinch of concassed parsley
- a pinch of powdered saffron
- a bit of bay
- a little savory and fennel
- 2 tablespoonfuls of oil
- cold water
- 1/3 oz. salt
- a pinch of pepper
- slices of household bread
- sections of spiny lobster

## Instructions

1. Cut the larger fish into slices; leave the smaller ones whole, and with the exception of the whiting and the red mullet, which cook more speedily than the others, put them all into a saucepan.
2. For two lbs. of fish, add one small onion, the chopped white of one leek, one small, peeled, pressed and chopped tomato, two crushed cloves of garlic, a large pinch of concassed parsley, a pinch of powdered saffron, a bit of bay, a little savory and fennel, and two tablespoonfuls of oil.
3. Moisten the fish with just enough cold water to cover it, and season with one-third oz. of salt and a pinch of pepper per quart of water.
4. Set to boil, and cook over a brisk fire.
5. At the end of eight minutes add the pieces of whiting and red mullet, and leave to cook for a further seven minutes.
6. Pour the liquor of the bouillabaisse over some slices of household bread lying on the bottom of a deep dish.
7. Set the fish on another dish with the sections of spiny lobster all round, and serve.
